# Offline mode: stub BQ-backed fetchers with empty DataFrames so the

def _bgg_link(game_id: int, name: str, year: int | None) -> str:
    year_part = ""
    if year is not None and not (isinstance(year, float) and pd.isna(year)):
        try:
            year_part = f" ({int(year)})"
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            year_part = ""
    return (
        f'<a href="https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/{int(game_id)}" '
        f'target="_blank" rel="noopener">{name}{year_part}</a>'
    )


def _img_tag(url: str | None) -> str:
    if not url or (isinstance(url, float) and pd.isna(url)):
        return ""
    return f'<img src="{url}" style="height:64px;width:auto;border-radius:4px;" />'


def _truncate(text: str | None, max_len: int = 220) -> str:
    if not text or (isinstance(text, float) and pd.isna(text)):
        return ""
    text = str(text).replace("&#10;", " ").replace("\n", " ").strip()
    if len(text) <= max_len:
        return text
    return text[: max_len - 3].rstrip() + "..."
```

# About

This report examines a classification model trained to predict whether a
user owns a game on BoardGameGeek. The model learns from features that
are observable about a game at release — its publisher, mechanics,
designers, playing time, and so on — and never reads BGG community
information like average rating or weight, so it can score newly
released games without leaking signal from the community after release.

::: {.callout-note}
To jump to the model's predictions for new and upcoming games, see the
[Predictions](#predictions) section.
:::

# Collection

The data in this project comes from BoardGameGeek. The unit of
observation is a game. We train a classification model at the user
level to learn the relationship between game features and games a user
owns — what predicts a user's collection?

## Games in Collection

The user's owned games, sortable by your rating, year, players, and
playtime.

```{python}
#| label: collection-table
#| column: page-right

def _fmt_range(lo, hi, suffix: str = "") -> str:
    """Render a min/max pair as 'lo–hi' or 'lo' when they're equal."""
    if lo is None and hi is None:
        return ""
    if lo is None:
        return f"{hi}{suffix}"
    if hi is None or lo == hi:
        return f"{lo}{suffix}"
    return f"{lo}–{hi}{suffix}"


def _format_collection(collection: pl.DataFrame, games: pl.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compact owned-games table: Image / Game / Year / Your rating /
    Players / Playtime / Weight. Filters to owned, sorts by user_rating."""
    if collection.height == 0:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    view = collection
    if games is not None and games.height > 0 and "game_id" in games.columns:
        meta_cols = [
            c for c in games.columns if c == "game_id" or c not in view.columns
        ]
        view = view.join(games.select(meta_cols), on="game_id", how="left")

    if "owned" in view.columns:
        view = view.filter(pl.col("owned") == True)
    if "user_rating" in view.columns:
        view = view.sort("user_rating", descending=True, nulls_last=True)

    pdf = view.to_pandas()
    if pdf.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame()

    def _safe(col, default=None):
        return pdf[col].tolist() if col in pdf.columns else [default] * len(pdf)

    ids = _safe("game_id", default=0)
    names = [
        n if isinstance(n, str) and n else (gn or "")
        for n, gn in zip(_safe("name", ""), _safe("game_name", ""))
    ]
    years = _safe("year_published", None)
    images = _safe("image", None)
    ratings = _safe("user_rating", None)
    min_p = _safe("min_players", None)
    max_p = _safe("max_players", None)
    min_t = _safe("min_playtime", None)
    max_t = _safe("max_playtime", None)
    weights = _safe("average_weight", None)

    def _fmt_rating(r) -> str:
        if r is None or pd.isna(r) or r == 0:
            return ""
        return f"{float(r):.1f}"

    def _fmt_weight(w) -> str:
        if w is None or pd.isna(w):
            return ""
        return f"{float(w):.2f}"

    def _fmt_int(x):
        if x is None or pd.isna(x):
            return None
        return int(x)

    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Image": [_img_tag(u) for u in images],
            "Game": [
                _bgg_link(int(g) if g else 0, n, y)
                for g, n, y in zip(ids, names, years)
            ],
            "Year": [
                "" if (y is None or pd.isna(y)) else str(int(y)) for y in years
            ],
            "Your rating": [_fmt_rating(r) for r in ratings],
            "Players": [
                _fmt_range(_fmt_int(lo), _fmt_int(hi))
                for lo, hi in zip(min_p, max_p)
            ],
            "Playtime": [
                _fmt_range(_fmt_int(lo), _fmt_int(hi), " min")
                for lo, hi in zip(min_t, max_t)
            ],
            "Weight": [_fmt_weight(w) for w in weights],
        }
    )


itables_show(
    _format_collection(data.collection, data.games),
    paging=True,
    pageLength=15,
    classes="display compact",
    columnDefs=[
        {"className": "dt-center", "targets": [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]},
        {"width": "90px", "targets": [0]},
        {"width": "60px", "targets": [2]},
        {"width": "90px", "targets": [3]},
        {"width": "80px", "targets": [4]},
        {"width": "100px", "targets": [5]},
        {"width": "70px", "targets": [6]},
    ],
    style="width: 100%",
    allow_html=True,
)
```

# Modeling

For each user we train a binary classifier whose target is whether the
user owns a given game. The training process examines historical games
and learns which features tend to co-occur with games a user owns.
Features are dummies indicating presence/absence of designers, artists,
publishers, plus continuous features for playing time, player counts,
and recommended minimum age.

::: {.callout-note}
The model only uses features observable at release. It does not consume
BGG community signals (average rating, weight, number of users rated)
so it can score upcoming games before the community has weighed in.
:::

## What Predicts A Collection?

::: {.column-margin}
Each bar shows how much a single feature pushes the model toward or
away from predicting "owned" — bars to the right of zero make
ownership more likely, bars to the left make it less likely. The
length is the strength of the effect.
:::

Beyond predictions, the model tells us *what* it learned. For a
penalized logistic regression the coefficients tell us, for each
feature, how much it shifts the log-odds of a user owning a game.
Positive values increase the probability; negative values decrease it.

```{python}

```{python}
#| label: top-games-training
def _eval_table(df: pl.DataFrame, top_n: int = 100) -> pd.DataFrame:
    view = df.head(top_n).to_pandas()
    ids = view["game_id"].tolist()
    names = view["name"].tolist() if "name" in view.columns else ["" for _ in ids]
    years = (
        view["year_published"].tolist()
        if "year_published" in view.columns else [None] * len(ids)
    )
    probs = view["proba"].tolist()
    rows = {
        "Rank": list(range(1, len(view) + 1)),
        "Game": [
            f'<a href="https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/{int(g)}" '
            f'target="_blank" rel="noopener">{n}'
            + (f" ({int(y)})" if y is not None else "")
            + "</a>"
            for g, n, y in zip(ids, names, years)
        ],
        "Pr(Yes)": [round(float(p), 3) for p in probs],
    }
    if "label" in view.columns:
        rows["Owned"] = ["yes" if bool(x) else "no" for x in view["label"].tolist()]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


itables_show(

    pageLength=15,
    classes="display compact",
    columnDefs=[{"className": "dt-center", "targets": [0, 2]}],
    style="width: 100%",
    allow_html=True,
)

## Top Games by Year

Side-by-side comparison of the model's top picks for each year. Cells
shaded blue are games the user actually owns (true positives).

```{python}
#| label: top-games-by-year
#| column: page-right
#| output: asis
all_eval = pl.concat(
    [arts.oof_predictions, arts.val_predictions, arts.test_predictions],
    how="diagonal_relaxed",
)

_eval_view = all_eval.with_columns(pl.col("year_published").cast(pl.Int64))
_eval_view = _eval_view.filter(pl.col("year_published") >= 2015)
_eval_view = _eval_view.with_columns(
    pl.col("proba")
    .rank(method="ordinal", descending=True)
    .over("year_published")
    .alias("_rank")
).filter(pl.col("_rank") <= 15)


def _truncate_name(text: str, max_len: int = 28) -> str:
    if not text:
        return ""
    return text if len(text) <= max_len else text[: max_len - 1] + "…"


if _eval_view.height == 0:
    print("No predictions in the eval splits to display.\n")
else:
    _years = sorted(int(y) for y in _eval_view["year_published"].unique().to_list())
    _name_pivot = (
        _eval_view.pivot(values="name", index="_rank", on="year_published")
        .sort("_rank")
    )
    _label_pivot = None
    if "label" in _eval_view.columns:
        _label_pivot = (
            _eval_view.pivot(values="label", index="_rank", on="year_published")
            .sort("_rank")
            .to_pandas()
            .set_index("_rank")
        )

    name_pdf = _name_pivot.to_pandas().set_index("_rank").fillna("")
    name_pdf = name_pdf[[str(y) for y in _years if str(y) in name_pdf.columns]]

    # Hand-render the table as raw HTML so we have full control over the
    # header (year columns only, no DataTables chrome, no sort arrows on
    # what should be static column headers).
    rows_html: list[str] = []
    rows_html.append('<table class="topn-by-year">')
    rows_html.append("<thead><tr>")
    rows_html.append('<th class="rank-col">Rank</th>')
    for y in name_pdf.columns:
        rows_html.append(f'<th>{y}</th>')
    rows_html.append("</tr></thead><tbody>")

    for rank in name_pdf.index:
        rows_html.append("<tr>")
        rows_html.append(f'<td class="rank-col">{int(rank)}</td>')
        for col in name_pdf.columns:
            val = str(name_pdf.at[rank, col]) if name_pdf.at[rank, col] else ""
            owned = False
            if _label_pivot is not None and col in _label_pivot.columns and rank in _label_pivot.index:
                truth = _label_pivot.at[rank, col]
                owned = bool(truth) if truth is not None else False
            cell_class = "owned" if owned else ""
            display = _truncate_name(val) if val else ""
            title_attr = f' title="{val}"' if val and len(val) > 28 else ""
            rows_html.append(
                f'<td class="{cell_class}"{title_attr}>{display}</td>'
            )
        rows_html.append("</tr>")
    rows_html.append("</tbody></table>")

    print("```{=html}")
    print("\n".join(rows_html))
    print("```")
```

# Predictions {#predictions}

## New and Upcoming Games

Predictions for recent and upcoming releases, generated by the deployed
model. Filtered to games published *after* the model's training window
(`finalize_through`). The **Status** column shows whether the game is
already in the user's collection.

```{python}
#| label: predictions-upcoming
#| column: page-right

# Build a per-game status from the user's collection. Priority:
# Own > Preordered > Wishlist > Want > Prev. Owned > —.
status_lookup: dict[int, str] = {}
if data.collection.height > 0 and "game_id" in data.collection.columns:
    coll_pdf = data.collection.to_pandas()
    for _, r in coll_pdf.iterrows():
        gid = int(r["game_id"])
        if r.get("owned", False):
            status_lookup[gid] = "Own"
        elif r.get("preordered", False):
            status_lookup[gid] = "Preordered"
        elif r.get("wishlist", False):
            status_lookup[gid] = "Wishlist"
        elif r.get("want", False) or r.get("want_to_buy", False):
            status_lookup[gid] = "Want"
        elif r.get("previously_owned", False) or r.get("prev_owned", False):
            status_lookup[gid] = "Prev. Owned"

# The model was trained on data through `finalize_through`, so anything
# published in or before that year is in-sample. "New and Upcoming"
# means strictly after.
finalize_through = arts.registration.get("finalize_through")
upcoming = (
    arts.upcoming_predictions
    .join(data.games, on="game_id", how="inner")
)
if finalize_through is not None:
    upcoming = upcoming.filter(pl.col("year_published") > int(finalize_through))
upcoming = upcoming.sort("predicted_prob", descending=True)


def _format_predictions_with_images(
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    top_n: int = 50,
    show_actual: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build an image+description-style predictions table for itables."""
    view = df.head(top_n).to_pandas()

    rank = list(range(1, len(view) + 1))
    images = view["image"].tolist() if "image" in view.columns else [None] * len(view)
    names = view["name"].tolist() if "name" in view.columns else [""] * len(view)
    years = (
        view["year_published"].tolist()
        if "year_published" in view.columns
        else [None] * len(view)
    )
    ids = view["game_id"].tolist()
    descs = view["description"].tolist() if "description" in view.columns else [""] * len(view)
    probs = (
        view["predicted_prob"].tolist()
        if "predicted_prob" in view.columns
        else view["proba"].tolist()
    )

    rows = {
        "Rank": rank,
        "Image": [_img_tag(u) for u in images],
        "Game": [_bgg_link(g, n, y) for g, n, y in zip(ids, names, years)],
        "Description": [_truncate(d) for d in descs],
        "Pr(Yes)": [round(float(p), 3) for p in probs],
        "Status": [status_lookup.get(int(g), "—") for g in ids],
    }
    if show_actual and "label" in view.columns:
        rows["Owned"] = ["yes" if bool(x) else "no" for x in view["label"].tolist()]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


itables_show(
    _format_predictions_with_images(upcoming, top_n=100, show_actual=False),
    paging=True,
    pageLength=10,
    classes="display compact",
    columnDefs=[
        {"className": "dt-center", "targets": [0, 4, 5]},
        {"width": "60px", "targets": [0]},
        {"width": "90px", "targets": [1]},
        {"width": "200px", "targets": [2]},
        {"width": "80px", "targets": [4]},
        {"width": "100px", "targets": [5]},
    ],
    style="width: 100%",
    allow_html=True,
)
```

def _format_eval_predictions(
    df: pl.DataFrame, *, top_n: int = 200
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compact eval-set predictions: Game | Year | Pr(Yes) | Actual."""
    view = df.head(top_n).to_pandas()
    rank = list(range(1, len(view) + 1))
    ids = view["game_id"].tolist()
    names = view["name"].tolist() if "name" in view.columns else [""] * len(view)
    years = (
        view["year_published"].tolist()
        if "year_published" in view.columns
        else [None] * len(view)
    )
    probs = view["proba"].tolist() if "proba" in view.columns else [0.0] * len(view)
    out = {
        "Rank": rank,
        "Game": [_bgg_link(g, n, y) for g, n, y in zip(ids, names, years)],
        "Pr(Yes)": [round(float(p), 3) for p in probs],
    }
    if "label" in view.columns:
        out["Owned"] = ["yes" if bool(x) else "no" for x in view["label"].tolist()]
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


itables_show(
    _format_eval_predictions(older, top_n=200),
    paging=True,
    pageLength=15,
    classes="display compact",
    columnDefs=[
        {"className": "dt-center", "targets": [0, 2]},
        {"width": "60px", "targets": [0]},
    ],
    style="width: 100%",
    allow_html=True,
)
```

# Model Details

Provenance for the model that produced these predictions.

```{python}
#| label: model-details
reg = arts.registration

def _short_sha(sha: str | None) -> str:
    return (sha or "")[:8] or "—"


def _short_dt(value: str | None) -> str:
    if not value:
        return "—"
    return str(value).split(".")[0].replace("T", " ")


def _maybe(value, fmt=str) -> str:
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and not value):
        return "—"
    try:
        return fmt(value)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return str(value)


metrics = reg.get("metrics") or {}
oof_overall = (reg.get("oof_metrics") or {}).get("overall") or {}

details = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ("User", arts.outcome and reg.get("username") or "—"),
        ("Outcome", arts.outcome),
        ("Candidate", f"{arts.selected_candidate} (v{arts.selected_version})"),
        ("Task", _maybe(reg.get("task"))),
        ("Tuning strategy", _maybe(reg.get("tuning_strategy"))),
        ("Splits version", _maybe(reg.get("splits_version"))),
        ("Trained through year", _maybe(reg.get("finalize_through"))),
        ("Decision threshold", _maybe(reg.get("threshold"), lambda v: f"{float(v):.3f}")),
        ("Train rows", _maybe(reg.get("n_train_used"), lambda v: f"{int(v):,}")),
        ("Validation rows", _maybe(reg.get("n_val"), lambda v: f"{int(v):,}")),
        ("Test rows", _maybe(reg.get("n_test"), lambda v: f"{int(v):,}")),
        ("Best params", _maybe(reg.get("best_params"), lambda v: ", ".join(f"{k}={vv}" for k, vv in v.items()))),
        ("Trained at", _short_dt(reg.get("trained_at"))),
        ("Finalized at", _short_dt(reg.get("finalized_at"))),
        ("Git SHA", _short_sha(reg.get("git_sha"))),
        ("Test ROC-AUC", _maybe(metrics.get("roc_auc"), lambda v: f"{float(v):.4f}")),
        ("Test PR-AUC", _maybe(metrics.get("pr_auc"), lambda v: f"{float(v):.4f}")),
        ("Test F1", _maybe(metrics.get("f1"), lambda v: f"{float(v):.4f}")),
        ("OOF ROC-AUC", _maybe(oof_overall.get("roc_auc"), lambda v: f"{float(v):.4f}")),
    ],
    columns=["Field", "Value"],
)

itables_show(
    details,
    paging=False,
    searching=False,
    info=False,
    classes="display compact",
    style="width: 100%",
    columnDefs=[
        {"width": "240px", "targets": [0]},
    ],
)
```
